A_general.open_code_note: Amplitude's public mcp-marketplace repository contains reusable skills, agents, and commands, not the hosted MCP server implementation. The mcp-server-guide repository is a setup guide. Neither is evidence of the code running at the endpoint.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com/mcp — EU residency endpoint for EU-region data.
https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp?discovery=progressive and https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com/mcp?discovery=progressive — optional progressive tool discovery on the respective regional servers.
Amplitude Docs MCP is a separate, read-only documentation server; it is not the analytics MCP endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Amplitude says MCP is available on every plan, including Free. Service accounts require an Enterprise plan and MCP access enabled; that is a separate authentication option, not a stated MCP usage charge.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Free plan: $0, no time limit, up to 2 million events/month. Plus starts at $0 and scales with event volume. Growth and Enterprise are custom-priced.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Pricing is for Amplitude platform usage and volume; the cited pages do not specify a separate MCP per-call fee. Free-plan volumes and capabilities are limited.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Amplitude account and OAuth are required. Org admins can disable MCP access. Per-project Use MCP (read/write) roles and product permissions constrain calls. Service accounts are Enterprise-only, read-only, and limited to 10 active accounts per organization. EU customers should use the EU endpoint.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization admin; project roles and permissions are assigned by organization admins.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with a Bearer challenge and protected-resource metadata URL. The provided metadata advertises an authorization server, DCR, authorization code with S256 PKCE, refresh, JWT bearer, token exchange, and scopes all:read/all:write. Amplitude documents AI Context text returned by get_amplitude_context, with organization/project context, terminology, metric definitions, and business rules. It also documents optional progressive discovery and a separate MCP App that renders charts in compatible clients.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The documentation identifies read and write operations; no tool-annotation fields are published. Write tools include taxonomy, experiment, metric, flag, dashboard, cohort, and Wave management. 2. Taxonomy deletes use a two-call confirmation flow with affected items/project/branch returned before the confirmed call; cohort syncs preview an export and ask for confirmation. The docs do not establish MCP Elicitation. 3. OAuth scopes are all:read/all:write; project RBAC separately enforces Use MCP (read/write) and product permissions. Org MCP access is enabled by default and admins can disable it. The tool list remains visible when a role lacks permission; calls fail at runtime. Service accounts are read-only, Enterprise-gated, capped at 10 active per org; token lifetime is not fixed in docs. 4. US/EU regional endpoints and optional progressive mode are documented; no read-only URL mode or tool-filter parameter is documented. Client-specific subsets exist, including an approximately 25-tool ChatGPT subset. 5. Access follows project permissions; replay tools describe searches from the last 30 days. No general PII masking/exclusion rule is documented. 6. Session replay search has a 30-day window; warehouse job page size is 1–100, default 25. No general rate limit or per-call cost is published. 7. Some schemas are documented in focused pages; broad validation/correction behavior is not. The consolidated-tools release says unresolved event/property names can return closest matching names. 8. MCP-specific logging, audit retention, and telemetry settings are not described. Taxonomy exposes activity history. 9. No feedback/rating tool appears in the official tool list. Documentation invites users to submit feedback via a form; the list includes a customer-data feedback analysis tool. 10. The server returns configurable AI Context; vendor-published marketplace skills are external files, not tools. Docs contain unverified client recommendations and workflow guidance. 11. Project AI Context is returned when requested; documentation does not say past agent behavior changes later tools or outputs. 12. US/EU endpoints and progressive dynamic discovery provide different tool exposure. Separate Docs MCP is read-only and not this endpoint. 13. No general raw API, arbitrary SQL, or script execution tool is listed. query_amplitude_data is a constrained analytics query tool.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Call this tool at the start of a session so the client applies your metric definitions, terminology, and business rules to later queries.
Call get_amplitude_context to confirm organization and project access.
Call list_tool_categories to see available product surfaces.

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The server supports progressive discovery, where only discovery tools and get_amplitude_context are initially listed and additional tool schemas are fetched by category. It also has separate US and EU endpoints.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code for the hosted server and no verbatim initialize/tool-schema payload; the official reference publishes names and descriptions but not the full definitions needed for the required character-count estimate.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Amplitude says MCP is not an event-ingestion endpoint; production/high-volume event sending uses an SDK or HTTP V2 API. The docs direct users to the UI for remaining gaps and to REST APIs or CLI for scripted workflows. The Guides and Surveys server lists/retrieves configuration; publishing is not listed there.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs advise clients to call get_amplitude_context at session start, discover categories and schemas in progressive mode, and use the returned business rules. These are client-facing recommendations; only documented tool workflows such as confirmed taxonomy deletes are described as server-side gates. The docs also recommend asking the user before certain actions, but no universal confirmation gate is specified.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Amplitude says its MCP uses existing permissions and project access controls, and that users gain no additional data access. Its AI FAQ states: “Under no circumstance will any AI partner use your data to train or improve their models.” It also says EU data remains in the EU for AI capabilities. These are product-level statements; the cited docs do not expose the enforcement implementation for each promise.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Amplitude describes MCP as GA and available on all plans. It says read/write permissions are enforced per project and that taxonomy deletes are confirmed in two steps. Its consolidated-tools release describes temporary chart edits being promoted server-side and closest matching names being returned when event/property names do not resolve.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Per-project permission enforcement, delete confirmation, and chart/cohort workflows are described as server behavior. General AI data-use, training, and residency statements are governance promises; no endpoint-level implementation details are public. Client instruction text and examples are not universal enforcement mechanisms.

contradictions: The protected-resource metadata advertises all:read and all:write, while the authorization-server metadata omits the client_credentials grant. Service-account documentation nevertheless instructs users to obtain tokens using grant_type=client_credentials.

The current official reference lists 45 distinct tools. Claude's third-party connector page lists 14 older names such as get_charts, get_context, and query_dataset, while the current official list uses consolidated names such as get_amplitude_charts and query_amplitude_data. Treat the directory list as an older/different client catalog, not as the current official list.

The official endpoint docs describe write tools generally, while service-account docs state that service accounts created through Settings are currently read-only. This is a credential-type restriction, not a contradiction in the endpoint's overall tool list.
observations_for_research: Progressive discovery changes the initially exposed catalog and retrieves schemas on demand; all supported tools remain callable after discovery.
Amplitude Context lets organizations and projects provide text that shapes later agent queries. Uploaded AI Controls files are not returned by MCP.

The consolidated-tools release says server-side workflows can combine multiple prior steps, such as promoting temporary chart edits, and return suggested real names when event/property names do not resolve.
The official repository distributes skills and agents separately from the hosted MCP service.
notes: Prepared pages/ and links.json were searched, including official tool references, focused setup pages, pricing/legal pages, catalogues, and endpoint checks. No hosted-server source code was found; the official marketplace repository is a skills/agents repository, not server code. Third-party catalogs are used only for comparison; Claude's tool list is older and INITE did not reveal names without sign-in. actions.json was checked against the official list: 45 distinct official names present, plus the three documented progressive tools; valid JSON, no duplicate names.
